Where it began

Dewald Brevis was born on 29 April 2003. He made his name at the 2022 Under-19 World Cup in the West Indies, where he made two hundreds and three fifties and was Player of the Tournament. His 506 runs beat the tournament record of 505 that Shikhar Dhawan had set.

Later that year, on 31 October 2022, playing for the Titans against the Knights at Potchefstroom, he made 162 from 57 balls. It was the highest T20 score made in South Africa up to then, and he reached 150 in only 52 balls, the fastest in T20 cricket at the time. He played his first first-class match for the Titans, against the Dolphins in Durban, in February 2023.

The player

He was an attacking right-handed batter in the middle order who could bowl a little leg-spin. His Test debut came on 28 June 2025, when he made 51 from 41 balls with four sixes. With Lhuan-dre Pretorius, a Titans team-mate also on debut, he put on 95 and pulled South Africa out of an early wobble.

By November 2026 he had played 4 Tests, with 138 runs at 23.00, two fifties and a best of 54. He had also taken one Test wicket, for 22 runs.

What made him special

Power, above all. He stood with an open stance, lifted the bat high and followed through hard, and he became known for no-look sixes, striking the ball and at once looking down at the turf instead of watching it fly. In August 2025 he made 125 not out from 56 balls against Australia at Darwin, beating Faf du Plessis's 119 to set a new high for South Africa in T20 internationals. In the Caribbean Premier League in 2022 he hit five sixes from five balls in a row.

His one-day international debut was brief, two balls for six runs, though nobody could fault the scoring rate.

Away from the middle

He took his T20 hitting all over the world. He was Rising Star of the 2025 SA20 season with MI Cape Town, and he helped MI New York to the title in the first Major League Cricket season in 2023, with 41 not out in the second qualifier. For Chennai Super Kings in May 2025 he made 57 from 23 balls against Gujarat Titans and was Man of the Match. At the 2026 T20 World Cup he made 207 runs as South Africa reached the semi-finals.

And finally

Most batters like to admire a big hit as it sails away. Brevis preferred to study the grass at his feet. Given where the ball tended to end up, he could probably afford to.
